subject: english-literature
title: Weather and Mood
welcome_lead: Storms, sunshine, fog — every weather word does mood work.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on pathetic fallacy and atmosphere.
final_note: You can now read mood through weather and atmosphere clues.

concepts.def: Mood of a scene or setting.

walkthroughs.body_html: When the sky 'wept' as a character grieves, the writer uses pathetic fallacy to align weather with feeling.
Use precise mood words: foreboding, serene, tense, joyful. Don't settle for 'sad' or 'happy'.
Imagery = strong word-pictures. 'Black clouds clawed the moon' builds a foreboding atmosphere through image.

What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.

mcqs.q: Why must students distinguish the narrator from the author?
options: The narrator is a constructed voice within the text; the author is the real person who created it. Conflating them misreads irony, unreliable narration and persona.
Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
The narrator's views are always the author's views.

mcqs.q: What is the function of dystopian fiction?
options: Dystopian fiction predicts what will actually happen in 100 years.
Dystopian fiction is just storytelling set in scary futures.
The narrator and author are different words for the same thing.
To critique tendencies in the writer's own society by extrapolating them into a nightmarish future — dystopias hold up a warning mirror to the present.
